scope: Saruhan core and Gediz basin source review
principles: Political control is distinct from settlement, fortress, route, and economic evidence.
Later Ottoman administrative boundaries are not used as 1326 province polygons.
Later conquests are not back-projected into the 1326 snapshot.
A source-supported city or fortress anchor does not by itself justify a surrounding territorial polygon.

anchors.name: Manisa
anchors.dateBasis: captured after a prolonged siege sometime after 1310; 1313 is widely used but TDV notes that the exact date is not established by a contemporary source
anchors.geometryPolicy: point/urban anchor only until reviewed historical extent exists

anchors.name: Akhisar
anchors.dateBasis: TDV states the city was probably first brought under Turkish rule by Saruhanoğulları active in Manisa region from 1300

anchors.name: Demirci
anchors.dateBasis: TDV places Demirci on the eastern side of Saruhan territory and records it as a separate appanage associated with Çuga Bey

anchors.name: Borlu
anchors.dateBasis: named by TDV among the eastern limits of the beylik

anchors.name: Adala
anchors.dateBasis: named by TDV among eastern limits of Saruhan territory

anchors.name: Turgutlu
anchors.dateBasis: named by TDV among the westward Saruhan domain; modern town identity must not be projected directly onto 1326

anchors.name: Nif/Kemalpaşa
anchors.dateBasis: TDV places Nif within Saruhan's western/eastern boundary description and states Saruhan gave Nif to his brother Ali Bey; independent research identifies a Saruhan/Aydın frontier across Nif Mountain
anchors.geometryPolicy: anchor plus frontier corridor; do not infer a large polygon

anchors.name: Gördes
anchors.dateBasis: appears in later Saruhan territorial tradition, but direct 7 April 1326 evidence is thinner than for Manisa/Akhisar
anchors.geometryPolicy: retain as review candidate, not canonical polygon

anchors.name: Menemen
anchors.dateBasis: TDV's Saruhan synthesis includes Menemen and the İzmir Gulf western shore among the beylik's western extent; exact 1326 local boundary requires further review
anchors.geometryPolicy: anchor; separate political control from coastal/trade function

anchors.name: Alaşehir/Philadelphia
anchors.dateBasis: TDV states that after a 1324 Germiyan attack the city was relieved by Andronikos II, then soon entered Aydinid protection, but remained the only Byzantine city in western Anatolia not conquered by Turks until Bayezid's 1391 conquest
anchors.geometryPolicy: Byzantine city anchor; do not assign to Saruhan in 1326

negativeEvidence.rule: Do not promote to Saruhan control in 1326 solely because it lies inside modern Manisa Province.
Do not use Umur Bey's 1335 conquest or Bayezid's 1390/1391 conquest as 1326 evidence.
Do not treat the modern district boundary as a medieval Saruhan polygon; the Nif Mountain frontier requires separate reconciliation with Aydın evidence.
